summary: Normalized the delivered VCF (Variant Call Format — the callset's row-oriented text record format) with `bcftools norm`, which splits multiallelic records (one row naming several alternate alleles) and left-aligns indels (insertions/deletions) against the GRCh38 reference genome. Across 4,968,537 records on the 195 canonical contigs, normalization split 66,639 multiallelic records into 133,278 rows and re-aligned the 39,913 alleles that split produced; zero bi-allelic (single-alternate) records changed spelling anywhere in the callset. The two candidate BUB1B alleles are single-base substitutions at bi-allelic sites, and both records were byte-identical in chromosome, position, reference and alternate allele before and after the run.
why: The oracle's scorer matches a submitted variant against the answer key by exact string equality on (chromosome, position, reference, alternate). An indel has more than one valid spelling, and a multiallelic record cannot be submitted as one row at all — so a biologically correct answer typed the wrong way would score zero. This is the first question asked about the data itself, and it has to be settled before any downstream join or submission can be trusted.
verdict: H008 — supported, committed at confidence 0.83: both BUB1B candidate alleles are canonical single-nucleotide substitutions, unchanged by normalization. The callset as a whole needed normalizing only at its 66,639 multiallelic sites; every bi-allelic record was already spelled the way `bcftools norm` would spell it.

inherits.what: the delivered VCF and the GRCh38 no-chr reference genome, fetched from the object store into scratch and byte-verified — step 1 cannot check a variant's spelling without both files present.

hands_to.what: step 2's coding-interval join and step 4's suppressed-call mining both join against variant coordinates, and a join against two spellings of the same variant silently loses rows; step 6's submission rows must be spelled exactly as the exact-match scorer requires.
